title: Clasp praise closer than craving
summary: The shabad contrasts the begging hand of desire with the Gurmukh who keeps the Lord's praise clasped to the heart. Choose nearness over the urge to acquire and be noticed.
takeaway: Trade the begging hand for the heart clasping praise.
lifeApplication: When desire reaches outward for proof, bring one phrase of praise inward and let it interrupt the grasping hand.

source.shortMeaning: The shabad contrasts the begging hand of craving with the Gurmukh who keeps the Lord's praise clasped to the heart.
source.lifeApplication: Before seeking proof from the room, ask whether the heart is reaching for more or holding praise near.

evidence.coreClaim: The line sets grasping desire against the greatness of keeping the Lord's praise in the heart.
evidence.turn: Craving loosens when praise becomes the nearer treasure.
evidence.practicalImplication: When desire reaches outward for proof, bring one phrase of praise inward and let it interrupt the grasping hand.
